title: Mumbai Cop Suspended After Viral Video Shows Threat to Plant Drugs on Student Protesters
excerpt: Constable Pawan Sangle was removed from his posting at Sion police station after footage emerged of him warning students they would be framed in narcotics cases if they continued to protest.
body:
Mumbai Police on Thursday ordered an inquiry into a viral video that allegedly shows a police constable threatening student protesters with fabricated drug charges, the latest flashpoint in a nationwide youth movement that has rattled the Indian government.

The widely circulated video purportedly shows constable Pawan Sangle, a driver attached to the Motor Vehicle Department and posted at Sion police station, warning students that drugs would be planted on them and that they would be booked under narcotics laws. "You'll spend the rest of your life in jail," he allegedly told the protesters, according to the Times of India.

"After verifying the facts, the driver concerned has been removed from his present posting till the completion of the inquiry."

— Mumbai Police official

Solidarity Protests Spread to Mumbai

The incident took place as Mumbai witnessed protests in solidarity with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led student agitation centered in New Delhi. The CJP, a movement that began as online satire in May, has channelled widespread youth frustration over repeated leaks of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) medical entrance exam papers, which affected some 2 million students.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2080201029828661713

Mumbai Police have already filed cases against more than 50 individuals tied to an unauthorized CJP solidarity protest at Chaityabhoomi in Dadar, according to officials. Protesters, including students, staged demonstrations demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan before being detained. Prohibitory orders banning public gatherings of five or more people without permission remain in effect across Mumbai through August 6.

National Movement Reaches Boiling Point

The Mumbai cop's suspension comes at a particularly volatile moment. On Monday, tens of thousands of mostly young protesters attempted to march on parliament in New Delhi and were met with tear gas and baton charges by Delhi Police. About 150 protesters were hospitalized with injuries, according to CJP leaders, while Delhi police reported 118 officers injured during what they termed "violent protests."

The crackdown did not disperse the movement. Protesters returned to their encampment at Jantar Mantar, a 300-year-old observatory that has served as the movement's headquarters, and rebuilt the makeshift camp that police had demolished the day before. Opposition parties, led by Rahul Gandhi's Congress, forced the suspension of parliamentary proceedings on Wednesday after demanding a debate on the exam leaks and police violence against students.

On Thursday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that "fast-track" courts would be set up to prosecute those behind exam paper leaks. "Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," Modi posted on X. The CJP responded by demanding Pradhan's resignation, signaling no intention to back down.

"If the government wants to talk, it has to come here now."

— Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder

Police Accountability Under Scrutiny

Sangle's threat to plant drugs on students has intensified scrutiny of law enforcement's handling of the protests. India has a troubled history of police planting evidence — including a 2022 case in which Mumbai Police officers were suspended after CCTV footage showed them planting drugs on a man during a raid in the Kalina area.

The student movement, which experts say represents a new wave of tech-savvy youth activism unaffiliated with traditional political parties, has drawn support from across India and abroad. Food deliveries from supporters as far as Kerala and the United States have poured into the Jantar Mantar protest site, sustaining the encampment even as monsoon rains drench the capital.

What to Watch

The outcome of the inquiry into Sangle's conduct will be closely watched as a barometer of police accountability during the protests. With opposition parties seizing on the CJP movement to corner Modi over an issue with massive resonance among India's youth — under-30s make up more than half the country's 1.42 billion population — the protests show no sign of abating. CJP leaders have vowed to remain at Jantar Mantar until Pradhan resigns, while the government has said it is willing to debate education reforms in parliament.
nri_angle: The NEET exam scandal resonates with Indian diaspora families whose children prepare for competitive entrance exams, and overseas supporters have sent food and supplies to protest encampments.
